title: The standard affine charts of a power of the projective line
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $n\ge1$, $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with structure morphism $q_1$, $X=(\mathbf P^1_S)^n=\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ the $n$-fold fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:X\to\mathbf P^1_S$ and $p_n:X\to S$. Let $\mathcal O(1)=\rho^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$, where $\rho:\mathbf P^1_S\to\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,T_1]$ is the second projection and $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ the twisting sheaf [def-pc-projective-space-twist] pulled back [def-pc-module-pullback], and write $T_0,T_1\in\Gamma(\mathbf P^1_S,\mathcal O(1))$ for the pullbacks of the coordinate sections. Put $\mathcal L_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1)$ (an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]) and $x_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_0$, $y_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L_i)$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $U_A=\bigcap_{i\in A}X_{y_i}\cap\bigcap_{i\notin A}X_{x_i}$, where $X_s$ is the open set where the section $s$ does not vanish. Then: (i) the $2^n$ opens $U_A$ cover $X$; (ii) for every affine open $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and every $A$, the open $U_A\cap p_n^{-1}(S')$ is affine, and the $R$-algebra map $R[Z_i\,(i\in A),W_i\,(i\notin A)]\to\Gamma(U_A\cap p_n^{-1}(S'),\mathcal O)$ from the polynomial ring in $n$ variables, $Z_i\mapsto z_i=x_i/y_i$, $W_i\mapsto w_i=y_i/x_i$ (the unique functions with $x_i=z_iy_i$ on $X_{y_i}$, $y_i=w_ix_i$ on $X_{x_i}$), is an isomorphism.

source.place: Constructions, Section (Tag 01ND, label section-projective-space): P^1_Z = D_+(T_0) ∪ D_+(T_1) with D_+(T_k) = Spec Z[T_{1-k}/T_k]; with Schemes, Lemma (Tag 01JR, open subschemes of a fibre product) and (Tag 01JQ, fibre product of affines is Spec of the tensor product), literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex

proof.text: *Charts of $\mathbf P^1_S$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] with $n=\{0,1\}$ to $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $q=q_1$. Write $D_0=D_+(T_0)_S$, $D_1=D_+(T_1)_S$ (preimages under $\rho$ of the standard opens of $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$), $t=u_{1/0}\in\Gamma(D_0,\mathcal O)$ and $s=u_{0/1}\in\Gamma(D_1,\mathcal O)$ (the pullbacks of $T_1/T_0$ and $T_0/T_1$). By (a), $\mathbf P^1_S=D_0\cup D_1$. By (b), for every morphism $g:Y\to\mathbf P^1_S$: $g^*T_1$ freely generates $g^*\mathcal O(1)$ over $g^{-1}(D_1)$ and $g^*T_0=g^*(s)\,g^*T_1$ there; $g^*T_0$ freely generates $g^*\mathcal O(1)$ over $g^{-1}(D_0)$ and $g^*T_1=g^*(t)\,g^*T_0$ there; and $D_k$ is the non-vanishing locus of $T_k$. By (c), for an affine open $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, $D_1\cap q_1^{-1}(S')$ is affine with $R[Z]\to\Gamma(D_1\cap q_1^{-1}(S'),\mathcal O)$, $Z\mapsto s$, an isomorphism, and $D_0\cap q_1^{-1}(S')$ is affine with $R[W]\cong\Gamma(D_0\cap q_1^{-1}(S'),\mathcal O)$, $W\mapsto t$. Since these opens are affine, each is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of its ring of global sections over $S'$, i.e. $D_1\cap q_1^{-1}(S')\cong\operatorname{Spec}R[Z]$ and $D_0\cap q_1^{-1}(S')\cong\operatorname{Spec}R[W]$ as schemes over $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text:
*The charts pulled back along the projections.* $\mathcal L_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (3), for $\xi\in X$ the value $x_i(\xi)=(\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_0)(\xi)$ is $T_0(\mathrm{pr}_i\xi)\otimes1\in\mathcal O(1)(\mathrm{pr}_i\xi)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathrm{pr}_i\xi)}\kappa(\xi)$, which is nonzero iff $T_0(\mathrm{pr}_i\xi)
eq0$ (a tensor product of nonzero vectors over a field extension), i.e. iff $\mathrm{pr}_i\xi\in D_0$ by step 1. Hence $X_{x_i}=\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(D_0)$ and likewise $X_{y_i}=\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(D_1)$. Applying step 1 to $g=\mathrm{pr}_i$: on $X_{y_i}$ the section $y_i$ freely generates $\mathcal L_i$ and $x_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*(s)\,y_i$, so $z_i:=\mathrm{pr}_i^*(s)|_{X_{y_i}}$ is the unique function with $x_i=z_iy_i$ on $X_{y_i}$ (uniqueness because $y_i$ is a free generator there); symmetrically $w_i:=\mathrm{pr}_i^*(t)|_{X_{x_i}}$ is the unique function with $y_i=w_ix_i$ on $X_{x_i}$. Consequently $U_A= igcap_{i\in A}\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(D_1)\cap igcap_{i
otin A}\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(D_0)$, an open subset, and the functions $z_i$ ($i\in A$), $w_i$ ($i
otin A$) are defined on all of $U_A$.

proof.text: *(i) The $U_A$ cover $X$.* Let $\xi\in X$. For each $i$, $\mathrm{pr}_i(\xi)\in\mathbf P^1_S=D_0\cup D_1$ (step 1). Put $A=\{i:\mathrm{pr}_i(\xi)\notin D_0\}$; then $\mathrm{pr}_i(\xi)\in D_1$ for $i\in A$ and $\mathrm{pr}_i(\xi)\in D_0$ for $i\notin A$, so $\xi\in U_A$ by the description of $U_A$ in step 2. Hence $X=\bigcup_{A\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}}U_A$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01NG (the cover D_+(T_0) ∪ D_+(T_1)); the combinatorial choice of A is written by the agent

proof.text: *$U_A$ over $S'$ as a fibre product of charts.* Fix an affine open $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and $A$. For each $i$ let $V_i=D_1\cap q_1^{-1}(S')$ if $i\in A$ and $V_i=D_0\cap q_1^{-1}(S')$ if $i\notin A$, open in $\mathbf P^1_S$ with $q_1(V_i)\subseteq S'$. Since $q_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_i=p_n$ for every $i$, step 2 gives $U_A\cap p_n^{-1}(S')=\bigcap_i\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(V_i)$. We claim that the canonical morphism $V_1\times_{S'}\cdots\times_{S'}V_n\to X$ (the fibre product of the $V_i\to S'$, mapped by the inclusions) is an open immersion with image $\bigcap_i\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(V_i)$, compatibly with the projections. Induction on $n$: for $n=1$ it is the inclusion $V_1\subseteq\mathbf P^1_S$ (and $p_1=q_1$). For $n\ge2$ write $X=X'\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ with $X'=(\mathbf P^1_S)^{n-1}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], first projection $a:X\to X'$, second projection $\mathrm{pr}_n$, and $\mathrm{pr}_i=\mathrm{pr}'_i\circ a$ for $i<n$. By induction $V'=\bigcap_{i<n}\mathrm{pr}'^{-1}_i(V_i)\subseteq X'$ is open, maps into $S'$ under $p_{n-1}$, and is $V_1\times_{S'}\cdots\times_{S'}V_{n-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] applied to $U=S'$, $V=V'$, $W=V_n$, the morphism $V'\times_{S'}V_n\to X'\times_S\mathbf P^1_S=X$ is an open immersion with image $a^{-1}(V')\cap\mathrm{pr}_n^{-1}(V_n)=\bigcap_{i\le n}\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(V_i)$, compatible with the projections. This proves the claim, so $U_A\cap p_n^{-1}(S')\cong V_1\times_{S'}\cdots\times_{S'}V_n$ over $S'$, the restriction of $\mathrm{pr}_i$ corresponding to the $i$-th projection onto $V_i$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01JR (label lemma-open-fibre-product) and the remark after it (V x_U W = V x_S W), Lemma Tag 01JS (label lemma-affine-covering-fibre-product); the induction over the factors is written by the agent

proof.text: *(ii) The fibre product of the charts is a polynomial ring.* By step 1, $V_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R[C_i]$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $C_i=Z_i\mapsto s$ for $i\in A$ and $C_i=W_i\mapsto t$ for $i\notin A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] applied $n-1$ times (the fibre product of the first $k$ factors being already $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the tensor product of their rings), $V_1\times_{S'}\cdots\times_{S'}V_n\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R[C_1]\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_RR[C_n])$, the $i$-th projection being $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the inclusion of the $i$-th factor, and by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-tensor-product] this ring is $R[C_1,\dots,C_n]$ with $1\otimes\cdots\otimes C_i\otimes\cdots\otimes1\mapsto C_i$. With step 4, $U_A\cap p_n^{-1}(S')$ is affine, isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}R[Z_i\,(i\in A),W_i\,(i\notin A)]$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and on global sections [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the variable $Z_i$ (resp. $W_i$) corresponds to the pullback along the $i$-th projection of the coordinate $s$ on $V_i$ (resp. $t$), i.e. to $\mathrm{pr}_i^*(s)=z_i$ (resp. $\mathrm{pr}_i^*(t)=w_i$) by step 2. So the $R$-algebra map $R[Z_i,W_i]\to\Gamma(U_A\cap p_n^{-1}(S'),\mathcal O)$, $Z_i\mapsto z_i$, $W_i\mapsto w_i$, is the composite of these isomorphisms, hence an isomorphism.
